{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wv-class-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"aa2b02b13f03370ed98b9c9b959cf16aec4818f5425f700862579e4f29c3a4ab","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wv-class-e:lineage:20","source_registry_sha256":"2261abaab8e2b1aaff5b8a336e3bfcf845adaa75847f0210442061783d7f9afb","source_liveness_sha256":"9a1fb68777f5e9d5c4b27899084cc233b265410fee506dfe6554447a61ea026e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Impaired driving","heading":"C2 — Confusables and KG hints, Impaired driving","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, Impaired driving

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
A blood alcohol concentration above point zero five percent and below point zero eight percent is only evidence of impairment, point zero eight percent or more is presumed DUI, and for a driver under twenty-one any measurable alcohol at all triggers zero tolerance [A01].
Why it matters: group bac-thresholds; difficulty high; prereq sec05-F10; confusables sec05-F08, sec05-F10 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A02
A first zero tolerance offense brings a thirty-day minimum revocation and no jail, while a second brings twenty-four hours in jail and sixty days or until the eighteenth birthday, whichever is greater [A02].
Why it matters: group zero-tolerance-penalties; difficulty high; prereq sec05-F17; confusables sec05-F17, sec05-F18 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A02
A first DUI below a point one five concentration carries a fifteen-day minimum revocation, whereas a first DUI at point one five or more carries forty-five days [A02].
Why it matters: group dui-penalties; difficulty high; prereq sec05-F19; confusables sec05-F19, sec05-F20 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A02
Second and third DUI offenses both carry a one-year minimum revocation, but jail rises from six to twelve months for the second to one to three years for the third, and the fine range doubles [A02].
Why it matters: group dui-penalties; difficulty medium; prereq sec05-F25; confusables sec05-F25, sec05-F26 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A02
DUI with child endangerment and DUI with bodily injury share the same fine range and sixty-day revocation, but the child endangerment jail minimum is forty-eight hours while the bodily injury minimum is twenty-four hours [A02].
Why it matters: group dui-penalties; difficulty high; prereq sec05-F21; confusables sec05-F21, sec05-F22 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A02
Refusing the breath test after a DUI arrest revokes the driving privilege for one year and up to life, a consequence of the implied consent law that is separate from any DUI penalty [A02].
Why it matters: group implied-consent; difficulty medium; prereq sec05-F13; confusables sec05-F13, sec05-F14 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A03
Interlock participation is optional for some offenders but mandatory after two or more DUI revocations within ten years, and applying before the revocation begins is what avoids the minimum revocation period [A03].
Why it matters: group interlock; difficulty medium; prereq sec05-F28; confusables sec05-F28, sec05-F29 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A01
Only time sobers a drinker, so coffee, exercise, fresh air and cold showers change nothing about the blood alcohol level [A01].
Why it matters: group alcohol-effects; difficulty low; prereq sec05-F05; confusables sec05-F04, sec05-F05 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A01
The whiskey shot, the six-ounce glass of wine and the twelve-ounce beer are equal in alcohol content even though they differ greatly in volume [A01].
Why it matters: group alcohol-effects; difficulty medium; prereq sec05-F06; confusables sec05-F06 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A03
About eighteen hours awake impairs driving like alcohol or drugs, yet a nap of only ten to twenty minutes can make a big difference when drowsiness strikes [A03].
Why it matters: group drowsy-driving; difficulty medium; prereq sec05-F30; confusables sec05-F30, sec05-F32 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A02
A DUI by a driver under eighteen revokes the license until eighteen or for the statutory period, whichever is longer, and every DUI revocation requires the Safety and Treatment program before reinstatement [A02].
Why it matters: group dui-penalties; difficulty medium; prereq sec05-F15; confusables sec05-F15, sec05-F16 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]
